metadata.title: The Last Duke
metadata.source: segmented from a Fabula-only package by gemini-3.8-flash

facts.statement: The regional tour operates under a crippling financial deficit caused by dwindling provincial ticket sales.
Roland Ghyll contracted Maisie Callow to replace Hester at half-salary to preserve the tour's budget and protect crew wages.
Hester Vane's right ring finger bears a permanent bloodless depression from eleven unbroken years of wearing Duke Malcor's iron ring.
The stage trapdoor counterweight in provincial touring theatres requires an actor's full bodily momentum to release without jamming.
Maisie Callow suppressed her own natural vocal register for six years out of fear of Hester Vane's punitive corrections.

premise.logline: A touring actor who has played the same villain for eleven years is told she will be replaced by the understudy she trained.

modules.theme: what is left of someone who has only ever been one part
modules.setting_time: the final three weeks of a long regional tour
modules.setting_place: a string of half-empty provincial theatres
modules.protagonist: a lead actor who has never missed a performance
modules.protagonist_want: to make the company regret the decision before closing night
modules.antagonism: a producer who thinks loyalty is a cost
modules.complication: the understudy is better than she was, and kinder
modules.ending_shape: she lets go of the part and keeps something truer

plot_shape.name: Transformation
plot_shape.central_question: Can this person become someone else, and what has to be shown to them first?

phases.name: The settled self
phases.purpose: The protagonist at their most characteristic, and what it costs others.

phases.name: Summons
phases.purpose: Something forces a confrontation the protagonist cannot argue with.

phases.name: Shown
phases.purpose: A sequence of confrontations, each harder to dismiss than the last.

phases.name: Refusal and collapse
phases.purpose: The last defence of the old self fails.

phases.name: The altered self
phases.purpose: The change tested against the situation from the opening.

cast_roles.purpose: The protagonist, defined by a habit the story will break.
Compels the confrontation; need not be sympathetic.
Bears the cost of the old self, visibly, from the first phase.
Notices the change before the protagonist claims it.

obligatory_moves: The opening establishes the exact behaviour the ending will contradict.
At least one confrontation shows the protagonist a consequence they caused and never saw.
The final phase revisits a specific person or place from the first phase.

events.summary: Hester finishes her performance as Duke Malcor to thin provincial applause, brutally scolding Maisie backstage for touching the prompt table.
events.dramatic_function: Establish Hester's obsessive, domineering habit of control and the unacknowledged toll it takes on Maisie.
beats: Hester delivers the final villainous soliloquy of Duke Malcor to a scattering of bored provincial patrons.
In the dressing room, Hester sharply rebukes Maisie for touching the prompt ledger without permission.
Hester rubs her hand and notes the deep groove pressed into her knuckle by Duke Malcor's heavy iron signet ring.

events.summary: Hester inspects the Dunmere stage mechanics, brushing aside Roland's grim warnings regarding the tour's mounting financial failure.
events.dramatic_function: Show the external fragility of Hester's position as Roland pushes back against her financial entitlement.
beats: Hester examines Dunmere's backstage trapdoor, testing the stiff counterweight mechanism that requires an actor's entire momentum to trigger.
Roland demands Hester accept lower billing and a reduced guarantee due to empty regional houses.
Hester dismisses Roland's warnings, declaring that provincial audiences only buy tickets to witness her signature role.

state_changes.value: terminate Hester's contract to balance the regional books

events.summary: Roland officially serves Hester notice that she is being replaced by Maisie for the final week at Crossbeck.
events.dramatic_function: Force the unavoidable crisis by formally notifying Hester of her replacement by Maisie.
beats: Roland presents Hester with a formal termination rider, stripping her of the role of Duke Malcor for the Crossbeck run.
Hester mocks the idea of an understudy carrying the show, but Roland reveals that Maisie has already accepted the lead contract.
Maisie cowers before Hester's outraged glare, keeping silent about why she accepted the promotion.

state_changes.value: sabotage Maisie's performance to retain the role of Duke Malcor

events.summary: At Crossbeck Civic Theatre, Hester confronts Maisie during private rehearsals and discovers the lasting vocal damage her mentorship inflicted.
events.dramatic_function: Confront Hester with the hidden damage her tyranny inflicted on Maisie's artistic confidence.
beats: Hester arrives early at Crossbeck to discover Maisie rehearsing Duke Malcor's soliloquy with unexpected subtlety.
Hester finds Maisie's private rehearsal notebook, documenting years of Hester's punishing vocal critiques and stifling corrections.
Maisie confesses in tears that years of Hester's reprimands forced her to strangle her natural voice into a harsh theatrical snarl.

events.summary: During Crossbeck blocking, Hester accuses Roland of staging a cheap usurpation, only for Roland to reveal Maisie took the cut-rate contract to save the company.
events.dramatic_function: Expose the truth of Maisie's sacrifice and shatter Hester's delusion of moral superiority.
beats: Hester interrupts the onstage run-through to mock Maisie's authority in Duke Malcor's heavy velvet mantle.
Roland reveals that Maisie only signed the contract at half-salary because he threatened to abandon the tour and leave the stagehands unpaid.
Hester stands humiliated before the stagehands, realizing her own wage demands had pushed the company to insolvency.

state_changes.value: shaken by the revelation of Maisie's sacrifice

events.summary: Hester watches Maisie's dress rehearsal from the dark wings and intervenes to save her from a dangerous trapdoor malfunction.
events.dramatic_function: Compel Hester to choose between her vindictive ego and Maisie's physical and artistic flourishing.
beats: Hester watches Maisie's climax from the wings, acknowledging that Maisie's vulnerability makes Duke Malcor genuinely tragic.
Maisie steps onto the Crossbeck trapdoor without applying the full body momentum necessary to release the stiff counterweight.
Hester lunges onto the backstage platform to throw the release lever manually, keeping Maisie safe from a violent fall.

state_changes.value: protect Maisie from harm and confront Roland

events.summary: Hester makes a desperate bid to buy back her closing night performance, but Roland refuses and forces her to accept the end of her reign.
events.dramatic_function: Break Hester's final transactional defense, leaving her stripped of her former identity.
beats: Hester offers Roland her entire personal tour savings in exchange for one final night as Duke Malcor.
Roland turns her down flat, explaining that Maisie's sacrifice secured the regional council subsidy and ensured the crew's future.
Hester breaks down backstage, realizing that her eleven years of ruthless stage possessiveness have left her completely isolated.

state_changes.value: stripped of pride and emotionally vacant

events.summary: In the Crossbeck dressing room before opening curtain, Hester surrenders Duke Malcor's ring and prompt ledger to Maisie with genuine grace.
events.dramatic_function: Demonstrate Hester's permanent transformation by having her voluntarily relinquish the role to Maisie.
beats: Hester invites Maisie into the dressing room and presents her with the prompt ledger, filled with gentle, encouraging notes.
Hester slides the heavy iron signet ring off her knuckle, staring at the deep, bloodless groove where the metal clamped her skin for eleven years.
Hester places the ring into Maisie's hand and takes her place quietly in the wings as Maisie commands the stage.

hidden_account.summary: Roland Ghyll accumulated severe operational debt across the provinces because audiences stopped buying tickets for Hester's repetitive performance.
Roland Ghyll coerced Maisie into signing a cut-rate contract to replace Hester at Crossbeck by threatening to abandon the tour and forfeit the crew's back pay.
